On Fri, Jan 21, 2022 at 2:46 PM Rosarie Tucci <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Hi Sophia -- sorry for the delay.We'rediscussing the Mis/Disinformation portfolio with Johnny next week on Tuesday
25 at 10:30am. At this meeting, we'll be doing a bit more mapping of possibilities and options -- so it just depends if you
would like to join as we discuss them or if you would prefer that we come with a few recommendations? If the latter, we
can set up a time on Thursday or Friday of next week.
On Wed, Jan 19, 2022 at 2:41 PM Sophia Lalani <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Rosarie - any luck on finding a time?
On Tue, Jan 18, 2022 at 12:08 PM Sophia Lalani <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Copy - thanks.
On Tue, Jan 18, 2022 at 11:41 AM Rosarie Tucci <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Let me connect with the team to make sure we have the right folks in the room (since this is a cross-
cutting portfolio) and we're teeing up the conversation so its most constructive.
We'll need to punt to next week to do that - so we'll find a time that works for everyone.
On Tue, Jan 18, 2022 at 11:37 AM Sophia Lalani <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Thanks, Colin. Dropping you to BCC
I think meeting to put together a plan is certainly in order. I have a number of open blocks Thursday and Friday
and happy to propose some times if folks' calendars are up to date.
On Tue, Jan 18, 2022 at 11:28 AM Colin Thomas-Jensen <[contact omitted]> wrote:
+ Sophia, who is going to run point for the front office on this issue.
I have been offline quite a bit for the past several days dealing with COVID-related issues, and here's a
summary from Gideon of SP's thinking on this from a meeting I missed last week.
"On the disinformation front - this just came up quite extensively in small group again today. this isn't clearly
bounded so part of this will be to figure out what we can usefully do. One piece of this will be understanding
what USAID's capabilities are. So that probably means engaging the DRG and ITR folks (maybe others) to
understand what we do in this space. And then it's probably a good idea to collect info on what we've
actually done (if anything) in places like Ethiopia, Ukraine, and Nepal to counter disinformation. This would
be mini-case studies to better understand what we do/ don't do. And then ultimately the bigger piece will be
the interagency -- SP wants to engage Jake to set up a process on this."
On Tue, Jan 18, 2022 at 10:57 AM Johnny Walsh <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Adding Meral, who I think would be our relevant team lead on this, and Diana who's been working the
interagency process on Information Integrity; there are others we could add as well. Yes we have some
capability, and yes it would be great to help the USG radically up its game on this. Maybe a meeting
among all of us would be in order, where you can elaborate on what SP said, and we can explain what we
have in play?
On Tue, Jan 18, 2022 at 10:41 AM Colin Thomas-Jensen <[contact omitted]> wrote:
hey Johnny and Ro -
Is there any inhouse expertise within the DG center on countering disinformation? SP pushing hard for
us to get an interagency process going on how the USG can get a LOT better at this and I am trying to
get a sense of what our capacity looks like to be a thought leader here.
Colin
Colin Thomas-Jensen (he/him/his)
